meiji_transition.summary: Kōchi Prefecture was set up in 1871 and absorbed Awa from 1876 to 1880.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Kōchi = Tosa Province, squeezed between the Shikoku mountains and the Pacific — long isolated, which gave it a temperament all its own.

history_timeline.title: Land of distant exile
history_timeline.summary: Tosa was a place of distant exile; Ki no Tsurayuki, governor of Tosa, wrote the 'Tosa Diary' (c. 935).

history_timeline.title: The emperor who chose exile
history_timeline.summary: In the Kamakura period Tosa was ruled by eastern vassals; after the Jōkyū War Retired Emperor Tsuchimikado volunteered for exile in Tosa and later moved to Awa.

history_timeline.title: The Hosokawa and the Tosa Ichijō
history_timeline.summary: Tosa's governors were the Hosokawa; during the Ōnin War the former regent Ichijō Norifusa took refuge at Nakamura in Tosa, founding the 'Tosa Ichijō' line.

history_timeline.title: Master of Shikoku
history_timeline.summary: Chōsokabe Motochika unified Shikoku with his part-time farmer-soldiers, the 'ichiryō gusoku', but submitted to Hideyoshi in 1585 and kept only Tosa.

history_timeline.title: Upper and lower samurai
history_timeline.summary: When Yamauchi Kazutoyo took over Tosa, the old Chōsokabe retainers were reduced to 'gōshi' (rural samurai), creating a rigid divide — the background to the rise of the gōshi Sakamoto Ryōma.

history_timeline.title: Freedom and People's Rights
history_timeline.summary: Sakamoto Ryōma brokered the Satsuma–Chōshū Alliance; in early Meiji Itagaki Taisuke launched the Freedom and People's Rights Movement from Kōchi.

specialties.name: Katsuo no tataki
specialties.note: Bonito seared over a straw fire

dialect.name: Tosa dialect
dialect.features: '-zeyo' and '-kini' became famous nationwide through dramas about Ryōma; a stubborn man is an 'igossō' and a spirited woman a 'hachikin'.

guide.opening: I'm a pilgrim — the Tosa stretch is the longest and hardest, called 'the dōjō of ascetic practice'. Sakamoto Ryōma grew up on this very coast gazing at the Pacific — want to hear his story?

regional_meme.title: Bekuhai drinking games
regional_meme.text: Kōchi people are legendary drinkers; at banquets they use 'bekuhai' cups with holes or pointed bottoms, so you can't put them down until they're empty.

regional_meme.title: Ryōma everywhere
regional_meme.text: Ryōma airport, Ryōma sweets, Ryōma statues… Kōchi's love of Ryōma is everywhere.

hero_persona.name: Sakamoto Ryōma
hero_persona.title: Rōnin of Tosa · broker of the Satsuma–Chōshū Alliance
hero_persona.opening_line: I'm Sakamoto Ryōma! Japan needs a good scrubbing — leave it to me to bring Satsuma and Chōshū together!
hero_persona.tone_prompt: bold, optimistic and broad-minded; ends sentences with Tosa dialect like '-zeyo' and '-kini'

ramen.highlight: Served piping hot in an earthenware pot — finish by adding rice to the broth

sake.taste_profile: Light & dry: the model of 'Tosa karakuchi', best with seared bonito
